title: GPU surge causing KV jounal corruption and slab fragmentation; runtime healing + graceful-shed rollout
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers across Hosted and Dedicated reported repeated GPU OOMs during bursty, long-context requests. Investigation shows the following correlated failure pattern: (1) a concurrent evict + checkpoint path produced inconsistent KV journal entries (missing tombstone markers), (2) the runtime allocator began scattering small survivor objects across slabs, escalating external fragmentation, and (3) under repeat pressure the GPU pool hit an OOM spiral that prevented normal compaction. The observed symptoms include silent KV lookup failures, incremental growth of per-session ephemeral allocations, and a persistent spike in free-list fragmentation metrics. Root-cause hypothesis: a race between async KV journal flush and slab reclaim which left journal segments partially written and produced inconsistent eviction metadata. When the evictor later tried to rehydrate state it created duplicate/abandoned handles that the allocator could not coalesce.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix deployed to Hosted canary (10%) without regressions for 48h
KV journal corruption rate (journal.checksum_errors) reduced to 0 in canary and <=1 per 10k evicts cluster-wide
GPU OOM incidents linked to this pattern reduced to zero for impacted customers for 7 days
New metrics and alerting added: kvcache.journal_corrupt, slab.rebalance_moves, allocator.external_frag_pct
Runbook updated and customer facing incident notes published
work_notes: 2026-02-27 18:04 - Oncall (S. Nguyen) triaged initial PagerDuty; affected: hosted-prod-us-west, dedicated-pool-11, private-vpc-ACME. Short-term mitigations: limited concurrent long-context sessions for the affected accounts and pinned legacy model variant as fallback.
2026-02-28 09:12 - Triage meeting with PM/Eng/SE. Assigned to Marco Rivera for runtime patch. PM (Aisha Patel) to coordinate customer comms and prioritization.
2026-03-02 15:40 - Engineering: added transactional append+checksum to KV journal (prototype). Unit tests for partial-write recovery added. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4982

2026-03-05 11:30 - Discovered allocator path root cause: small ephemeral allocations bypassing slab coalescer. Implemented an incremental slab rebalancer to migrate cold allocations to consolidated arenas. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5016
2026-03-08 02:20 - Canary rollout started on hosted-canary-1 (10%). Observed one journal_corrupt event early, auto-healed by the new compactor. No customer-facing failures.
2026-03-10 20:05 - Expanded canary to 40% after 72h stable; coordinated with Dedicated infra to apply hotpatch to reserved nodes during maintenance window (2026-03-11).

2026-03-12 09:00 - Post-canary checks: allocator.external_frag_pct down 32% on nodes with rebalancer; GPU OOM alerts for affected customers suppressed. Preparing rollout plan for full fleet and private customers.
Notes: follow-up tasks include: (a) extra fuzz tests for journal partial-writes, (b) integration test for eviction+checkpoint race, (c) add metric to surface per-tenant slab skew
playbook: Short-term: 1) throttle long-context session concurrency for impacted tenants, 2) enable fallback to smaller-context model variant, 3) apply hotpatch with KV journal checksums and compactor to affected pools. Long-term: release runtime-2026.03.1 with slab rebalancer and additional telemetry; add proactive eviction diagnostics.
rollout_plan: Dedicated reserved nodes: maintenance window 2026-03-11 02:00-04:00 UTC (apply hotpatch)
Private customers: ship patch bundle and coordinated upgrade guide; target windows agreed with 3 customers by 2026-03-20
